Deutsche Bank
FTE interview experience 2024
Anisha Pravin Jadhav
B.Tech in Computer Engineering
Deutsche Bank visited our campus in the first week of August 2023 to hire final-year
students for the role of Graduate Technical Analyst.
Details
●CTC: 19.63 LPA
●Role: Graduate Analyst
●Eligibility: CGPA above 7; No Backlogs; CS, IT & EXTC branch
Hiring Pattern
●Online Coding Test
●Technical Interview - 1
●Technical Interview - 2
●Professional Fitment interview
●HR interview
Online Coding Round :
●Platform: Proctored on HackerEarth
●Date: 4th August 2023
●Questions: 3 with partial test case marks
●Duration: 1.5 hours

●3 coding questions
●Question-wise difficulty: Easy - Medium - Medium
●Question-wise scoring: 20 - 50 - 50
●Partial marking was present if you were only able to clear some test cases
1.
Power Limit - 20 marks [Solved by brute force]
Given two resources with powers A and B respectively. At each second, you have
to select one resource out of the two to run the software. The power of the
resource at the time of selection should be greater than 1. Every second, the
power of the selected resource gets reduced by 2 and the power of the
unselected resource gets increased by 1. The software stops when at least one
resource has a power of 0.
You are given integers A and B. Print the maximum number of seconds your
software can run if you select the resources optimally as output.
Sample input: 3 5
Sample output: 6
Passed 9/10 test cases.
2. Auto Suggest - 50 marks [Solved by DP]
Given a dictionary consisting of N words and a query word S. All the words and
The query word S consists of lowercase alphabets only. You need to auto-suggest
the best word from the dictionary that is closest to S. Two words are first
compared by their Levenshtein distance to the word S. If two words have the
same Levenshtein distance, then the lexicographically smaller word is given
2

priority.
Levenshtein Distance is defined as the minimum number of edits required to
convert one string to another. Operations allowed to edit are insert, delete or
replace a character.
Input: N words S
Output: suggested word
Passed all test cases.
3. Backlink Sorting - 50 marks [created 2 dictionaries sorted one and used it]
You are given N webpage titles and corresponding arrays that constrain the
number of backlinks for each webpage. The objective is to rank the web pages in
descending order based on the number of backlinks they have. If two or more
pages have the same number of links then maintain their ordering.
Sample Input:
4
pg1 pg2 pg3 pg4
20 80 40 10
Sample Output:
pg2 pg3 pg1 pg4
Passed 6/10 test cases.
40 students were shortlisted for interviews held on 9th August 2023 in offline mode in
TPO seminar hall. So we were supposed to reach the TPO seminar hall at 8:30 am in
formals.
3

Technical Interview 1: (1 hr 10 mins)
I was the first to be interviewed and was a bit nervous as it was my first offline interview.
But the interviewer was so warm and helpful. She first greeted me and then gave a quick
self-introduction of her.
●
Tell me about yourself
●
As I mentioned in my interview I’m a self-motivated person, so she asked me what is
self-motivation, how you are self-motivated, and in the future how will you stay
motivated.
●
I answered very honestly and she was very satisfied and impressed with my answer.
That big smile on her face gave me confidence and then we moved on to the main
interview.
●
What are the all subjects you have covered so far?
●
Which was your favorite subject so far?
●
Asked me for some Python functions.
●
Then she asked about AI & ML, what is the difference between AI, ML & data
science?
●
How chatgpt works?
●
Also, she asks about the working of recommendation systems using ML.
●
What is the difference between Linux and Windows? Why do you prefer Linux over
Windows?
●
OOPS concepts with real-life examples.
●
What is data structure and types of data structures?
●
After that, she wanted to test my presentation skills, so she asked me to explain
anything I was fluent with on the whiteboard. So I explained the data structures. I
started by explaining basic array data structure from scratch, then she asked me to
explain vector, stack, queue, recursion, etc., and the difference between each of
them.
●
Explain what is palindrome and write code in any language. I explain all brute force
to optimized solution.
4

●
Asked SQL queries on student tables starting from basic to advanced. (insert,
update, delete, alter, join, union, intersection, nested queries, grant, revoke, etc.)
●
Asked about some OS concepts such as virtual memory, paging, some networking
commands, scheduling, etc.
●
What will you do if you have a different opinion from your team member while
working on a project?
●
Which database do you prefer SQL or no-SQL? Explain types and differences.
●
Why DB?
Asked if I had any questions:
My questions were,
●
As she mentioned earlier she has experience in other 3 companies previous to DB, I
asked what is different in DB compared to others.
●
What difficulties do you face while working in DB?
●
What is the work culture of DB and techstack used?
●
How does DB manage all the finance-related work and maintain a top rank in
industries?
It lasts for 1 hour. Out of 41, 35 were shortlisted for the second technical round.
Technical Interview 2: ( 50 mins )
He was so rude and grilled me so badly that after returning back from the interview cabin I
knew that I was not going to be selected for the next round. Even I packed my bag. But then
I got selected for the next round. So never lose hope.
●
Introduce yourself from birth to 10th std without mentioning any education
qualities or things not mentioned in your resume in 2 minutes.
●
Asked about my hobbies and which authors' books I like to read.
●
Which is my favorite subject?
5

●
Ask me to code any program in any language it should have a real-life example.
●
Difference between Linux, Redhat, and Ubuntu, then compare it with Windows.
●
List all the Linux commands you know (asked for the implementation of some)
●
Told me to list all the memory units I knew in ascending order.
●
Asked me which memory can be accessed fastest by CPU and then gave me various
options and asked me to order them ( RAM, CD, Hard disk, cache something like
that)
●
Asked me how a small RAM can run a large program, and I answered using virtual
memory, then he asked me to explain what virtual memory is.
●
Asked me about paging and segmentation and to state different types of page
replacement algorithms. Gave a numerical for optimal page replacement.
●
List all the git commands you know, then he asked some follow-up questions like
can you create a branch of the branch, etc.
●
Asked about S3 buckets and EC2 instances as I mentioned in my resume.
●
Which company provides the online services platform, name them with their
owners.
Asked me if I had any questions.
●
How does it feel to work in DB?
●
On which technology is DB focused?
●
What is your role in DB?
●
How do you manage your work life and personal life?
Lasted for about 50-55 mins. 26 were shortlisted for the next round.
Professional Fitness Interview: (35 minutes)
●
Introduce but include something not on the resume.
●
How was your day till now? Are you tired?
●
Tell about your internship experience and the project done there (explained the
entire project in depth).
6

●
Ask a program (I didn’t remember it) to explain first then code it on paper then
further add complexities to it.
●
What are your hobbies and what do you do other than studies?
●
What is AWS and how do you use it in your projects?
●
How does it feel to work with a team?
●
Answer the response to the situation.
●
You are working in a team and team members are having issues with their opinion.
But you have to make a quick decision. What will you do or how will you handle the
situation?
●
If the company asks you to work each weekend for 6 months and you don’t get any
compensation for it. what would you do? Will you do that work?
●
Which database is good MongoDB or MySQL?
●
Ask about my family background.
●
Are you comfortable with relocation?
●
Have you any plans for higher education?
Then he asked if I had any questions for him.
My questions were,
●
How DB is best for freshers?
●
How was your experience till now in DB?
●
What issues do you face while starting a career in DB?
Lasted 35 min. All shortlisted for profit were asked to give the HR round.
HR Interview: (25-30 minutes)
●
Introduce yourself.
●
Internship discussion. what did you learn, Highlight some learning you gained
excluding technical and overall Experience.
●
Why DB?
7

●
What are the values of DB?
●
Where do you see yourself in 5 years?
●
Are you comfortable with relocation?
The interview ended at 7:10 p.m. It was pretty good. At last, she asks if I have any questions
for her.
My questions were,
●
Why DB is mass hiring when other companies are reducing placement drives due to
the recession?
●
How does it feel to work in DB and its working environment?
●
Why it is a good company to start a career for freshers?
●
One good and bad thing about DB?
●
What issues do she face while joining DB?
Lasted 25 - 30 min
All 26 candidates were selected.
Tips:
●
Be consistent with your coding and theory subject knowledge. Don't ignore theory
subjects they are as important as coding so study thoroughly for theory subjects.
●
Be very thorough with every single line on your resume, your work in the projects
you’ve done, and the challenges/learnings of each of them.
●
Don’t lie on your resume. As if you got caught then it’s a bad impression on your
interviewer.
●
Be prepared with your introduction other than your educational qualities.
●
I daily practice coding questions from the online platforms. I prefer leet code for
coding questions, geeks for geeks for ease of explanation of questions, and hacker
rank for SQL questions.
8

●
Do a well-rounded research about the company before the interview, you should
have a working knowledge of what the company does.
●
Be confident and don’t be nervous. The interviewer also knows that you don’t know
everything, what they expect is that you should know everything in detail which is
mentioned in your resume.
●
At last, it only depends on your interviewer and your luck.
●
Never lose hope. Trust yourself. Everything will happen just wait for the right time
and be consistent in your studies.
●
I wasn’t able to get any internship for some reason, but I decided to work hard. For
the placement drive, DB was the first company I was interviewed and guess what, I
was selected. So never lose hope and don’t stop. Keep doing it consistently.
All the best!! You can do it!! :)
If you have any queries, feel free to drop an email at jadhavanisha3033@gmail.com
